risks.note: The CFO states the Indian Rupee witnessed sustained depreciation pressure against the US Dollar in FY 2025-26, driven by global inflationary concerns, elevated US interest rates and geopolitical instability, which directly increased input costs for a business that imports critical components.
risks.risk: Rupee depreciation against the US Dollar

risks.note: Management describes Aztec as a business that 'sources a meaningful proportion of its critical components from international suppliers', so currency and supply-chain movements flow straight into procurement economics. This import dependence is the explicit rationale for the backward-integration and indigenisation programme.

The CFO flags cautious capital spending by end-customers and states that customer decision-making cycles lengthened during FY26, with capital expenditure approvals slowing - a direct constraint on new printer sales, which are capex purchases for customers.
risks.risk: Cautious customer capital spending and lengthening decision cycles

risks.note: Elevated global inflationary pressures and rising procurement costs are named as one of the three converging realities that defined FY 2025-26, pressuring margins on equipment and consumables.

Geopolitical instability in West Asia and consequent volatility in crude oil prices are cited as drivers of the currency and cost pressure; crude is also relevant to solvent and ink raw-material inputs for the consumables business.
risks.risk: Geopolitical instability and crude oil volatility

risks.note: FY26 involved a deliberate investment cycle in manufacturing, technology, digital infrastructure and strategic acquisitions; the CFO acknowledges headline consolidated PAT appears marginally lower year-on-year, with depreciation on the new Kanera facility having commenced. Returns depend on ramping these newly built capabilities.
risks.risk: Execution risk on a heavy, self-funded investment cycle

risks.note: The Chairman states that as Aztec grows, developing a future-ready workforce and a strong leadership pipeline 'will be one of our highest priorities', with continued investment needed in technical, R&D, manufacturing, digital and sales/service skills - a structural constraint for a 122-person organisation scaling into manufacturing and IP ownership.

The Chairman frames the aspiration as building products in India that 'can compete confidently with established global technologies', acknowledging that Aztec's move from distribution to proprietary technology puts it against entrenched multinational coding and marking players.
